title: Creamy Lardon, Leek and Mushroom Penne
subtitle: White wine & tarragon cream · ready in about 45 minutes
description: Crisp lardons, soft leek, garlic and mushrooms in a white wine and tarragon cream sauce, with the penne finished in the pan.

steps.text: Heat a little {{oil}} in a large, deep pan and fry the {{lardons}} until mostly cooked.
Add the {{leek}} and {{garlic}} and fry, breaking the leek rings apart as they soften.
Add the {{mushrooms}} and fry until cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the {{penne}} in boiling water until just short of al dente. Scoop out and keep a mug of the pasta water before draining.
steps.note: Aim for 1–2 minutes less than the packet time — it finishes cooking in the sauce.

steps.text: Pour the {{wine}} into the sauce and let it bubble until mostly evaporated.
Stir in the {{cream}}, {{tarragon}} and a good grind of {{pepper}}, then simmer gently.

Tip the drained {{penne}} into the sauce and stir over the heat until it's cooked. Loosen with splashes of the reserved pasta water until the sauce is as thick as you like, then season with {{salt}} to taste.

notes: Lardons are already salty, so taste before adding any salt at the end.
Get the pasta water on while the lardons fry so the penne is ready around the time the sauce has simmered.

nutrition.note: Rough estimate assuming double cream and smoked lardons; single cream will bring the fat and calories down a lot.
